title: The birth of the daily commute
text: Commuting {{1}} become such an accepted part of working life that few of us question it. Yet {{2}} the invention of the railway, most people simply lived within walking distance {{3}} their workplace. Trains changed everything, allowing workers to travel {{4}} the suburbs into city centres each morning. Today, although many of us dream {{5}} working from home, the majority still make the daily journey. Transport experts argue {{6}} this will only change if employers become more flexible. Whatever happens, it seems unlikely {{7}} the morning rush hour will disappear completely {{8}} our lifetime.

gaps.explanation: Present perfect: commuting has become — 'it' would need 'it has become' after 'commuting' as subject.
'Before the invention of the railway' — time reference to an earlier period.
'within walking distance FROM their workplace' — from marks the starting point.
travel from A to B — from marks the origin of the journey.
'argue that + clause' — introduces the reported claim.
The conjunction 'that' links 'it seems unlikely' with the following clause.
